mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL inflation index exceeds +0.5 percentage points, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to investor risk aversion to rising prices.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year rolling window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect disappears when controlling for FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2,000 jobs over three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly average > current quarter mean + 2,000 for 3 months
failure_condition: Empirical power of the signal falls below 0.2 (IC) in periods of high unemployment or weak wage growth, or the effect is not significant after including GDP growth and earnings momentum controls.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 5 points over two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates soft earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly average < previous month mean - 5 for 2 months
failure_condition: The signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in backtests during periods of strong demand or high consumer confidence, or IC < 0.1 regardless of regime.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months, it signals a housing recovery that drives optimism in large-cap equities, producing a positive S&P 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: The effect is not robust across different housing cycle phases or is reversed when adjusted for mortgage rates and consumer sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 3% for 4 consecutive months, in the absence of a concurrent rise in UNRATE, predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as lower policy rates reduce discounting of future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly < 3% for 4 months and UNRATE monthly <= previous month mean
regime_hint: Low-rate environment with stable labor costs
failure_condition: The signal fails to predict returns when unemployment is rising or when inflation surprises are positive, or IC < 0.15 after controlling for credit conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 5% in a single month accompanied by a simultaneous decline in PAYEMS of 1% suggests weak consumer demand, which is associated with a negative S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly < previous month mean - 5% and PAYEMS monthly < previous month mean - 1%
failure_condition: The interaction is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during periods of strong retail sales or when consumer confidence is high, or IC remains below 0.2 regardless of trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in GDPC1 (GDP expenditure) of at least 2% over two consecutive quarters, when accompanied by a sharp drop in INDPRO of 8 points, predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals economic softening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly < previous quarter mean - 2% and INDPRO quarterly < previous quarter mean - 8 points for 2 quarters
failure_condition: The signal fails to predict returns when demand proxies are also weak or when the economy enters a recession with a sharp drop in unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising by at least 0.25% per month for 3 months), the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs and reduced equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly > previous month mean + 0.25% for 3 months
failure_condition: The effect is not observed when inflation is falling or when the yield curve steepens, or IC > 0.2 in tightening periods.
